input.quote: 14.1 Assignment. Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights or obligations hereunder, whether by operation of law or otherwise, without the prior written consent of the other party. Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party shall have the right to assign this Agreement in connection with the merger or acquisition of such party or the sale of all or substantially all of its assets related to this Agreement without such consent, except in the case where such transaction involves a direct competitor of the other party where consent of the other party will be required.
input.rationale: Section 14.1 is mutual and already carries a successor carve-out (merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets without consent) and a consent requirement for other assignments, and there is no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right anywhere (Sections 11.1-11.2 contain only non-renewal, breach and insolvency triggers), so this is not walk-away territory. It nevertheless fails the fallback on two material terms: consent is at each party's absolute discretion with no "not unreasonably withheld" standard (which matters most where Commerce One asserts an acquirer is a "direct competitor"), and there is no written-notice mechanic for successor assignments. We target the fallback rather than the asymmetric preferred position because rewriting this mutual clause into a Vendor-only restriction would require collateral changes; the missing affiliate carve-out and competitor limb are noted but not pressed at this level.

mappings.quote: Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights or obligations hereunder, whether by operation of law or otherwise, without the prior written consent of the other party.

mappings.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.

proposal.summary: Add a reasonableness standard to assignment consent and a written-notice requirement for successor assignments in Section 14.1.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 14.1 requires the other party's consent to any assignment with no reasonableness standard, so consent could be withheld arbitrarily. We have added the customary "not unreasonably withheld" standard and a written-notice requirement for successor assignments, consistent with our fallback position; the rest of the section is unchanged.

ops.oldText: Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights or obligations hereunder, whether by operation of law or otherwise, without the prior written consent of the other party.
ops.newText: Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights or obligations hereunder, whether by operation of law or otherwise, without the prior written consent of the other party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld.

ops.oldText: except in the case where such transaction involves a direct competitor of the other party where consent of the other party will be required.
ops.newText: except in the case where such transaction involves a direct competitor of the other party where consent of the other party will be required, provided the assigning party gives the other party written notice.
